confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are based on aggregated cost-of-living figures found by web search (Numbeo data published by Expatica around June 2026, MyLifeElsewhere and Expat Arrivals): inexpensive meal about £15, mid-range three-course meal for two about £65-66, cappuccino about £3.45, domestic draught beer about £4.90-5.30. The cocktail anchor uses Expatistan's crowd-sourced figure of about £9 from October 2025 and a general guide range of £8-12, so it is moderately uncertain. Wine is based on a general guide range of £5-8 per glass, which is not clearly dated, so it is less certain. The searches did not return a GBP/USD rate, so GBP was converted at an assumed rate of about 1.34 USD per GBP for July 2026, which adds roughly ±5% uncertainty. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. They allow for higher July summer and event-season demand in Cardiff and are the least certain anchors. The RBA figure is the 18 Nov 2026 rate of 0.6720 (16 Nov 0.6759, 17 Nov 0.6742), but a search summary reported it, citing the RBA's daily table. The RBA page itself was not opened, so the figure is unconfirmed.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink prices are based on Cardiff-specific aggregated data. Accommodation is benchmarked against mid-sized UK regional cities such as Bristol, Newcastle and Leeds, where Cardiff is usually close to or slightly below their summer room rates.
